::: {.callout-note}
## Relationship to The Geometry of Motion (GoM)

This workspace (THC — Tangent Hyperplane Contraction) and the [Geometry of Motion series](../The_Geometry_of_Motion/quarto/index.html) (GoM) cover overlapping content but serve different purposes:

- **THC** is an 8-chapter focused textbook workspace developed for the AffineDrift website, emphasizing practical control design, implementation, and validation checklists. Chapters are concise and web-first.
- **GoM** is a broader 3-volume academic series (Mathematical Primer + Foundations + Transverse Control) developed as a formal LaTeX manuscript with full proofs. Volume I overlaps significantly with THC in topics.

Neither supersedes the other. THC is the more practical, website-oriented reference; GoM is the more rigorous academic manuscript. Cross-references between the two are intentional.
:::

## Introduction and Qualitative Purpose

This workspace organizes a textbook-scale treatment of nonlinear control centered on one unifying viewpoint: tangent-space dynamics are the common language of stability, optimality, and physical interpretation in high-dimensional systems.

The goal is to move from article-style notes to a coherent, chaptered manuscript that supports both practitioners and researchers. The writing strategy is to pair rigorous equations with explanatory interpretation and implementation guidance.

## In Laymans Terms

The project asks a practical question: how do we make complex motions both high-performing and repeatable? The answer is to track how tiny errors evolve, design feedback using those error dynamics, and certify that those errors shrink.

## Geometric Intuition

A nonlinear trajectory is a curve on a manifold. At each point on that curve, a tangent space gives a local linear picture. Metrics act as local rulers in these tangent spaces. Contraction theory asks whether those locally measured deviations shrink, while optimal control chooses feedback that reshapes those deviations toward task goals.
